items.title: Toronto mayor says Eglinton Crosstown LRT won't open within next month
items.description: Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Chow said there would be an update on the status of the rapid transit line next month, confirming it would not be open to the public before.

items.title: Canada's 2030 climate target far out of reach, according to Environment Canada data
items.description: Canada's legally binding climate target seems to be out of reach, according to new data released from Environment and Climate Change Canada.

items.title: International students allocated to Ontario colleges, universities to drop again
items.description: Since applying a cap on international students at the beginning of 2024, the federal government has been reducing the number of applicants each year.

items.title: What does U.S. want from Canada to renew CUSMA? Trump's trade rep has list
items.description: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told members of Congress this week that next year's joint review 'will depend on the successful resolution' of several issues.

items.title: Chanthy Yen brings contemporary Cambodian cuisine to Vancouver with TOUK
items.description: Canada’s first restaurant of its kind opens downtown.

items.title: Vancouver International Black Film Festival returns for its fifth edition
items.description: A hybrid lineup of films, panels, and workshops spotlights creators from Canada and around the world.

items.title: Making lawyers swear Oath of Allegiance to monarch unconstitutional: Alberta court
items.description: The Appeal Court's three-judge panel has declared the Oath of Allegiance requirement unconstitutional and of no force or effect, meaning it is no longer required in Alberta.

items.title: Manitoba Government Announces Removal Of 23 Grocery Property Controls
Quebec school insurers set new sledding hill standards
items.description: New guidelines outline how school snowbanks should be built for sledding, including height, slope, supervision and when helmets may be required.

items.title: Eby Is Under Fire for Undermining the Rule of Law
items.description: Lawyers say the premier’s criticism of rulings on Indigenous rights reflects ‘a troubling trend.’

items.title: RCMP not aware of fentanyl in illegal cannabis in Nova Scotia, despite premier's claims
items.description: The Nova Scotia RCMP says it's not aware of any fentanyl-laced cannabis being sold by unauthorized cannabis retailers in the province, after the premier made this claim in a news conference last week. The claim raises tensions with Mi'kmaw communities amid a province-wide crackdown aimed largely at on-reserve cannabis dispensaries.

items.title: Eli Wood's mom is 'imploring you to please help' find the Kitchener, Ont., 25-year-old as reward offered
items.description: Eli Wood, 25, went missing on Oct. 19 after a fire at his Kitchener, Ont., home. Police say foul play is suspected in the disappearance of the Wilfrid Laurier University student. Now, his family is offering a $5,000 reward for information about his whereabouts.

items.title: Snow fun allowed? Winter play guidelines for some Quebec schools spark backlash
items.description: Some Quebec schools are being encouraged to follow a long list of rules for playing on snow mounds, including the possibility of forcing kids to wear helmets, sparking yet another debate about whether child safety fears have gone too far.

items.title: Saskatchewan town remains without drinking water with restoration date unknown
items.description: Residents of Outlook, Sask. could remain without safe drinking water for several days, with an official saying it's "difficult to say" when access will return.

items.title: Toronto man charged with defrauding 28 investors of $6.6M
items.description: A Toronto man has been charged for allegedly defrauding 28 investors of $6.6 million they provided to trade in foreign exchange following an Ontario Securities Commission investigation.

items.title: Boats run aground in Vancouver's False Creek after overnight windstorm
items.description: A number of boats ran aground in Vancouver's False Creek early Wednesday morning amid a windstorm, and it's led to calls for governments to step up and deal with the problem of derelict boats along the water body.

items.title: #TheMoment boats decked out in Christmas lights lit up the Newfoundland coast
items.description: Joyce Morgan, chairperson of the Boat Lighting Committee, tells The National about the moment over 50 boats decked out in Christmas lights lit up Port de Grave, N.L.
